marks.gloss_en: לא, אבהמה -- 'not permitted' refers to the animal (= p_baraita_al_habehema; its two defences at 2b.2 are objections against that prop)
the baraita's 'though he is not permitted' refers to the [mother] animal, not to the fetus
אמר רב אשי: תא שמע, רבי יהודה מתיר בשבורה מפני שאינה יכולה להתרפאות; הא יכולה להתרפאות אסר, והא עובר נמי כיכול להתרפאות דמי. שמע מינה
R' Yehuda permits only what cannot be healed, and a fetus is like one that can be healed -- so the fetus is not 'damaged' in his sense
R' Yehuda permits a damaged animal because it cannot be healed
והא 'דמיו' קתני! -- the baraita says 'its (masc.) value', i.e. the fetus (kind tanya under protest: the formula is והא קתני on the baraita just cited)
תני 'דמיה' (= p_tni_dameha)
והא 'נותן כל דמיו לכהן' קתני, ואי בהמה -- כהן מאי עבידתיה? (kind tanya under protest, as above)
הכא במאי עסקינן: he gave him a pregnant animal to fatten; מיגו דקנסינן ליה אבהמה, קנסינן ליה אעובר (= p_okimta_meuberet_lefatma)
read [in the baraita] 'its (fem.) value', not 'its (masc.) value'
לימא מתניתין דלא כרבי יהודה, דתנן: רבי יהודה מתיר בשבורה! -- the mishna's prohibition on selling a fetus seems not to be R' Yehuda's
אפילו תימא רבי יהודה: שבורה לאו היינו אורחיה, עובר היינו אורחיה (= p_shvura_lav_orcheh)
the mishna's 'though he is not permitted' [to sell the fetus] can be R' Yehuda's
תא שמע: והנותן לו בקבלה אף על פי שאינו רשאי -- מאי לאו אעובר?

לא, אבהמה -- defended at 2b.7 against two challenges: והא דמיו קתני -- תני דמיה; והא נותן כל דמיו לכהן -- a pregnant animal given to fatten, fined for the fetus by extension (p_okimta_meuberet_lefatma). The defence is not representable as structure (header).
R' Yehuda: one who receives an animal from a gentile [in receivership] and it gave birth -- they assess it and he gives half its value to the priest
תא שמע: R' Yehuda permits a damaged animal because it cannot be cured -- so one that can be cured is forbidden, and this is like one that can be cured. שמע מינה
R' Yehuda permits [selling] a damaged animal [to a gentile], because it cannot be cured
תא שמע: והנותן לו בקבלה -- ולא קתני אף על פי שאינו רשאי

ולטעמיך: המשתתף לו is also not so marked -- is it then permitted? But Avuha diShmuel forbids partnership with a gentile! אלא (2b.20): it taught sale and the same holds for partnership and for receivership; ומאי שנא מכירה דנקט -- דעיקר מכירה היא
Avuha diShmuel: a person may not form a partnership with a gentile, lest he owe him an oath and swear by his idol
תא שמע: והנותן בקבלה אף על פי שאינו רשאי ... מאי לאו אבהמה? (3a.1)
R' Yehuda: one who receives an animal from a gentile and it gave birth -- they assess it and he gives half its value to the priest
והתניא: they said to R' Yehuda, don't they breed it and it gives birth! -- so [the Rabbis'] reason is its offspring, not confusion
the Rabbis' reason [for forbidding a damaged animal] is that it will be confused with a [whole] animal
הכי קאמרי ליה: our reason is confusion; the breeding argument was aimed at YOUR reason (it cannot be cured, like one sold for slaughter)
you permit because it is like one sold for slaughter -- but they breed it and it gives birth, and so he keeps it!
לכשתלד -- it does not accept a male
R' Yehuda to them: when it gives birth [we will consider it] -- it does not accept a male
and the Rabbis say: as long as the gentile's hand is in the middle, it is exempt from the firstborn law
here the case is one who gave a pregnant animal [to the gentile] to fatten: since we fine him for the animal, we fine him for the fetus
selling an animal [to a gentile] for its fetuses is forbidden
selling an animal [to a gentile] for its fetuses is permitted
